tools.name: upper_list_drivers
tools.description: List the active drivers on the Upper team that owns the API token: id, name, email and phone. Use the ids with upper_assign_drivers and upper_share_route_to_drivers. GET /ext-get-drivers.

tools.name: upper_list_stops
tools.description: List the team's stops in optimized order: address, coordinates, contact, time window, duration, status, route_id and custom ids. Pass route_id for one route (optionally scheduled=true/false); pass unscheduled=true (without route_id) for stops not on any route; with no filter all active stops are ret

tools.name: upper_get_optimization_status
tools.description: Check whether a route is optimized: status is optimized, pending (still running) or not_optimized, plus the queue_id of the last job. Poll this after upper_optimize_route. GET /ext-optimization-status.

tools.name: upper_get_custom_fields
tools.description: The workspace's five stop custom-field slots (custom1 - custom5: type, label, enabled, required) and which are enabled. Needs the Custom fields feature in the Upper plan. GET /ext-get-custom-fields.

tools.name: upper_get_capacity_fields
tools.description: The workspace's five capacity-field slots (capacity1 - capacity5: label, unit, enabled) used for load planning. GET /ext-get-capacity-fields.

tools.name: upper_create_route
tools.description: WRITE: create a new, empty route (name, date, optimization preference, units, pickup sequencing, service time). Omitted settings fall back to the account's defaults. Returns the new route_id; add stops with upper_create_stop. Calling it twice creates two routes. POST /ext-create-route.

tools.name: upper_update_route
tools.description: WRITE: change settings of an existing route (name, date, optimize_for, units, pickup_settings, service_time). Only the fields you pass change. POST /ext-update-route.

tools.name: upper_create_stop
tools.description: WRITE: create a stop. The address is geocoded by Upper. Pass route_id to put it on a route (the route must not be active/in progress; an optimized route is flagged for re-optimization); omit it for an unscheduled stop. Calling it twice creates two stops. POST /ext-create-stop.

tools.name: upper_update_stop
tools.description: WRITE: change an existing stop; only the fields you pass change. A new address is re-geocoded (city/state/zipcode you pass with it are ignored); city/state/zipcode apply only without an address. Passing route_id moves the stop to that route. Editing a stop on an optimized route flags the route for r

tools.name: upper_assign_drivers
tools.description: WRITE: assign one or more drivers (ids from upper_list_drivers) to a route, replacing the route's drivers. Every id must be an active driver on the team. If the route was already optimized it is reset to unoptimized (needs_optimization: true), so run upper_optimize_route again. POST /ext-assign-driv

tools.name: upper_optimize_route
tools.description: WRITE: start optimizing a route's stop order. The route needs at least one stop and one assigned driver (upper_assign_drivers). It runs asynchronously: this returns status pending and a queue_id, then poll upper_get_optimization_status. If a job is already running, that job is returned. POST /ext-op

tools.name: upper_share_route_to_drivers
tools.description: WRITE: push a route to the drivers' mobile app NOW, which sends each driver a notification. Without driver_ids the route's assigned drivers are used; with them, every id must be an active driver on the team. Sending twice notifies twice. Confirm with the user before calling. POST /ext-share-to-drive

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "upper_share_route_to_drivers" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: WRITE: push a route to the drivers' mobile app NOW, which sends each driver a notification. Without driver_ids the route's assigned drivers are used; with them,…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: upper_list_drivers · Private data: upper_list_drivers, upper_list_stops · Public sink: upper_list_drivers, upper_create_route, upper_update_route, upper_create_stop, upper_update_stop, upper_assign_drivers, upper_optimize_route, upper_share_route_to_drivers · Destructive: upper_assign_drivers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: upper_list_drivers · Private data: upper_list_drivers, upper_list_stops · Public sink: upper_list_drivers, upper_create_route, upper_update_route, upper_create_stop, upper_update_stop, upper_assign_drivers, upper_optimize_route, upper_share_route_to_drivers · Destructive: upper_assign_drivers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
